adaptation: Calendar order; Gapminder uses numeric five-year steps, not malformed strings.
finding: Lexical and numeric year order agree.
chart_choice: A line uses position on an ordered calendar axis to show a trend.

adaptation: Compare row number with the actual year for one country's time series.
finding: All steps are equally spaced, so the shape is unchanged; the year axis communicates the five-year unit.
chart_choice: Paired line panels isolate the same country series while making the x-axis units explicit.

adaptation: Population is a stock, so show totals and per-country means separately.
finding: A sum is a continent total, not a daily or monthly flow.
chart_choice: Two line panels separate total population from per-country mean; their units and questions differ.

adaptation: Compare a centered and trailing 3-observation smoother.
finding: The trailing curve ends later because it excludes future observations.
chart_choice: Observed values and rolling lines compare ordered time without hiding the window.

adaptation: Scan all available year starts and 3-, 5-, and 7-point windows.
chart_choice: A line shows the complete record; a computed window scan tests framing sensitivity.

adaptation: Check observed time coverage instead of inventing a partial month.
finding: Gapminder records 12 five-year snapshots from 1952 to 2007.
chart_choice: A line preserves the observed five-year sequence and makes absent monthly data explicit.

adaptation: Use continents as mutually exclusive population parts, not product lines.
finding: The stacked total is world population; no volatility claim about products is made.
chart_choice: A stacked area is legal because each country belongs to one continent and totals are additive.

adaptation: Compare legal continent GDP parts as a pie and sorted bars.
finding: The five continent totals sum to the world total; bars improve ranking.
chart_choice: A four-slice pie shows the whole; sorted bars use length for precise ranking.

adaptation: Show total GDP and continent GDP shares in separate panels.
finding: Shares describe composition; the world total is not shown on a second axis.
chart_choice: Separate line panels avoid a dual axis while comparing world total and component shares.
